name: plate_bounding_box
why: «Does it fit in the 300x260x40 box» is the other question asked before ordering, and the answer is from where to where the part reaches on each of the three axes. The six extremes of a centred 100x100x20 plate are exact numbers: -50/+50 in X and in Y because it is centred, 0/+20 in Z because the extrusion starts from the sketch plane and goes forward.
_why_the_real_points: they are taken with GetExtremePoint in six directions and not with GetBodyBox, which is declared APPROXIMATE for non-planar surfaces and can be larger than the part. A bounding box declared larger than the true one makes everything around it be sized wrong: the box to ship it in, the part next to it, the pocket it has to fit into.

expect.tolerance_why: the extremes are read in metres and multiplied by a thousand
with a single body, the box of the body and that of the part are the same

expect.why: the limit is declared at every call: this is not the smallest possible box, and whoever packs must know it
